top_choice_rationale: P001 (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) rewards the discovery that changed the field: proglucagon processing, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, its glucose-dependent action and extrapancreatic effects, which defined what any therapy had to mimic and led to a drug class with confirmed outcome benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Mature, three-name limit respected, and the citation can name the therapeutic consequence. Mojsov's priority remains contested, so P002 (Knudsen in the third seat) is a defensible second, since long-acting analogue design was a real step; both rank far above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to the GLP-1 candidates (my work is nuclear receptors and dopamine neurons)
